clue.text: The better or the other half

definitions.text: The better or the other half

parts.words: The better or the other half
parts.note: both 'better half' and 'other half' are jokey names for the person you are married to

explanation.definitionFit: A husband or wife is called one's better half or other half in everyday idiom.

clue.text: The farmer's one, without having to put on an act !

definitions.text: The farmer's one, without having to put on an act !

parts.words: The farmer's one, without having to put on an act
parts.note: a farmer grows food, and a theatre impresario stages a show without acting in it

explanation.walkthrough: A farmer is a food maker, and the theatrical sense puts on plays without acting in them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who grows crops or stages plays is called by this word.

clue.text: Tune sung badly ? They're balmy!

indicators.note: something done badly comes out wrong, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A song is sung out of tune, and the singers must be barmy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balmy' suggests 'barmy', mad, but here means like a balm.
explanation.definitionFit: Ointments are soothing balms.

clue.text: Being unprepared, is pro tem in difficulties in the river

indicators.note: the second in places the rearranged phrase inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England

indicators.note: in difficulties suggests trouble, so the Latin phrase is jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone caught unready for the moment is in trouble in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pro tem' (for the time being) is jumbled by 'in difficulties' and set inside a Devon river named by 'in' the second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking off the cuff, without preparation, is speaking impromptu.

clue.text: What's driven the, bird to the merry-go-round?

parts.note: a car is the thing a motorist drives
an ousel (ouzel) is the blackbird or ring ouzel

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what drove a bird onto a fairground ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's driven' reads as 'what has driven' the bird, but it is a noun phrase: the thing that is driven, a CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground roundabout with rising horses is a merry-go-round.

clue.text: The landscape gardener has what it takes-colour

parts.note: capability is having what it takes to do something
brown is a colour

explanation.surface: A garden designer is talented and has a particular colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancelot 'Capability' Brown designed many great English country-house parks in the 18th century.
explanation.definitionFit: This 18th-century English designer laid out parks such as Blenheim's.

clue.text: Sketch from the departure platform ?

parts.note: a rough drawing read as the line of travel going out from a station platform

explanation.walkthrough: The word for a rough drawing splits as a railway line for trains going out.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough plan or drawing of the main features is a sketch.

clue.text: Biscuits straight from the oven — what a picture !

parts.note: ginger snaps are thin crisp biscuits
food fresh from the oven is hot

explanation.surface: Freshly baked biscuits make a lovely sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what a picture' sounds like admiration, but it is the definition: a quick photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A quickly taken photograph is a kind of picture.

clue.text: A letter for mine host ?

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lets property is a letter; mine host is an old phrase for an innkeeper.

clue.text: Sporting position of the man who, came to dinner

definitions.text: the man who, came to dinner

explanation.definitionFit: A fielding place behind the wicketkeeper in cricket; also a guest who stays a long time, like the title character of the play The Man Who Came to Dinner.

clue.text: Win in the regatta in fine style

indicators.note: the first 'in' says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A crew comes first at the rowing regatta with plenty of style.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'regATTA IN'; 'in fine style' just completes the picture of a stylish victory.
explanation.definitionFit: To win something is to achieve or gain it.

clue.text: "She is the fairies' midwife

parts.note: a line from Mercutio's speech in Romeo and Juliet about the queen of the fairies who brings dreams

explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet Mercutio calls this tiny dream-bringing queen the fairies' midwife.

clue.text: Silent about the decoration

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stays quiet on the subject of the ornaments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of', but it signals the rearrangement of SILENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Glittering strips hung on a Christmas tree are a typical decoration.

clue.text: Used Anthony to roll when in drink ?

definitions.text: Used Anthony to roll when in drink ?

parts.words: Used Anthony to roll when in drink
parts.note: the novelist Anthony's surname begins with 'troll', an old verb meaning to roll or to sing a round over drinks, so the question asks whether he used to do that

explanation.walkthrough: To troll the bowl was to pass the drinking cup round; the clue reads the Victorian novelist's surname as if it described such a habit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian novelist Anthony who wrote the Barsetshire novels has this surname.

clue.text: An actor's property or a child's ?

definitions.text: An actor's property or a child's ?

parts.words: An actor's property or a child's
parts.note: a stage prop is an item for acting with, and a toy is a child's thing to play with

explanation.definitionFit: A toy is a child's object for games, and a stage prop is an object used in a play.

clue.text: Flag of many colours

parts.note: the flag is the wild flower of that name, and the many colours are those of the rainbow, which the same word names in Greek myth

explanation.definitionFit: The yellow flag is a wild species of this flower, which is named after the Greek goddess of the rainbow.

clue.text: I have — longings in me" (A and C.)

definitions.text: I have — longings in me" (A and C.)

parts.words: I have — longings in me" (A and C.)
parts.note: Cleopatra's words before her death in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra, with the missing adjective meaning undying

explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra's line 'I have immortal longings in me' gives the word meaning deathless.

clue.text: Where yachtsmen may be found lacking in respect ?

parts.note: in, as in on the water of
the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England, famous for sailing

explanation.surface: A clue asks where sailors are, and adds that they are rude.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the sailing water off Cowes; being 'in the Solent' gives the word for rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude and disrespectful behaviour is insolent.

clue.text: Boss of the breeding establishment

explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised knob or nailhead; a farm where horses are bred is also called by the same word.

clue.text: Unflappable quality of certain potentates

parts.note: calm composure, also the title 'Serene Highness' used for some princes

explanation.definitionFit: Calm composure is an unflappable quality, and some princes are addressed as 'Your Serene Highness'.

clue.text: A potential source of glue, aunt ?

definitions.text: A potential source of glue, aunt ?

indicators.note: potential means not yet formed, so the two words are reshaped into something new

explanation.surface: Someone asks their aunt whether something could be made into glue.
explanation.walkthrough: GLUE and AUNT rearranged give a hoofed animal, whose hooves were boiled down for glue.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoofed mammal such as a horse was a traditional source of animal glue.

clue.text: What milady's drier will do in high-pressure conditions

definitions.text: What milady's drier will do in high-pressure conditions

parts.note: a hair drier both warms the hair and sets it in curls

explanation.walkthrough: 'High-pressure conditions' points to weather, where a hot spell often comes with high pressure; the hair drier warms and curls.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell of very hot weather, often under a high-pressure system, is described by these words.

clue.text: Terribly anti getting lit up in one's stockings

indicators.note: in places the short reversed word inside the stockings

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone very much against getting drunk in their stockings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lit up' looks like drunk, but in this down clue 'up' turns the word backwards before it goes inside old-fashioned stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Being strongly against something is being antagonistic.

clue.text: Player has to return out of the alien wood

indicators.note: here out of means on the outside of, so the reversed short word wraps the foreign wood
return says the short word is turned round

parts.note: bois is French for a wood, so a foreign wood

explanation.surface: A musician must come back from a strange forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' turned round gives OT, which wraps BOIS, the French word for wood, to give O-BOIS-T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the oboe is a musical player.

clue.text: To flatter the grocer won't bring it down, however

definitions.text: To flatter the grocer won't bring it down, however

parts.words: the grocer won't bring it down, however
parts.note: read literally, the grocer keeps the price of a dairy spread up rather than reducing it

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for flattering, read as a shop notice, says the price of a dairy spread has risen.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay on compliments is to flatter someone, in an idiom about spreading something smooth.

clue.text: Canned pie perhaps from the gents outfitter ?

definitions.text: Canned pie perhaps from the gents outfitter ?

parts.words: Canned pie perhaps from the gents outfitter
parts.note: a pie jumbled and put into a tin gives a piece of men's jewellery sold at an outfitter

explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters of PIE inside TIN make the item; the clue gives no separate word for TIN, so it is read as a cryptic description.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin worn to hold a necktie in place is sold at a men's clothing shop.

clue.text: First novel

explanation.definitionFit: Something earliest, not a copy, is first; something new and fresh is novel.

clue.text: He follows the pious ink-slinger

parts.note: the reformer Martin is said to have thrown his inkpot at the devil, and a follower of his church is named after him

explanation.walkthrough: Legend says Martin Luther threw an inkwell at the devil, so the pious ink-slinger is the reformer.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Protestant church founded on Martin Luther's teaching is his follower.

clue.text: Old Faithful, for instance

parts.note: a famous hot spring in Yellowstone that erupts at regular intervals

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the word also means a gas water heater, but Old Faithful is the Yellowstone spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Faithful is the best-known example of a spouting hot spring.
